# Infinite vs Noah: whose customer, whose account


Noah and Infinite look similar from a distance — one API for stablecoins beside fiat, named accounts, SWIFT, wide corridors. The differences are in the primitives. On Infinite, each customer holds an individually titled demand deposit account at chartered, FDIC-insured partner banks, stablecoin custody sits inside a bank's perimeter, onboarding runs in your brand end to end, and moving money that belongs to your customers is the design center.


By[Nikhil Srinivasan](https://infinite.net/company/about) , Founder & CEO


·


Last updated Aug 10, 2026

TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. Noah offers long-tail payout corridors, virtual accounts with SWIFT support, and built-in verification.
2. Infinite issues each customer a real demand deposit account with its own account and routing numbers, not a virtual account number.
3. On Infinite, each Wallet Account is established and controlled by a chartered partner bank, and its keys never leave the bank's custody perimeter.
4. Noah's standard model onboards end users directly as its own customers, while Infinite's hosted flows keep onboarding in the platform's brand.
5. Infinite treats third-party funds flows as the design center, closing first-time reviews that traditionally take around 30 days in one to two days.


01


## Two similar surfaces


Noah has assembled real breadth: long-tail payout corridors including emerging-market local rails, virtual accounts with SWIFT support, and built-in verification. Among stablecoin payment APIs, it is a serious platform, and much of what this essay says about primitives applies to the whole category — Noah included — rather than to any one provider's failing.


02


## Virtual account numbers, or titled DDAs


Much of the market issues named virtual accounts: deposit details in the customer's name that route into the provider's structure. Infinite issues[real demand deposit accounts](https://infinite.net/platform/managed-account) — each customer's own account with its own account and routing numbers, established at chartered, FDIC-insured partner banks,[not a sub-ledger on a pooled account](https://infinite.net/learn/glossary/virtual-account) . The distinction matters when auditors, banking partners, or regulators ask where the funds actually sit and whose name is on the records.


03


## Custody: omnibus balances, or the bank's perimeter


A common model in this market holds customer funds in omnibus structures — balances the provider holds for the benefit of its users. Infinite's[Wallet Account](https://infinite.net/platform/wallet-account) takes the other path: a bank-owned wallet per customer, established and controlled by a chartered partner bank. Your customer holds the balance; the bank holds the wallet and its keys, which never leave the bank's custody perimeter — nothing for your team to secure, rotate, or lose.


04


## Whose brand your customer sees


Under many provider models, your customers also become the provider's customers — they accept the provider's terms and hear from the provider directly. Noah's public terms, for example, provide that users may not submit orders on behalf of a third party; its standard model onboards end users directly as its own customers. On Infinite,[hosted flows carry your brand end to end](https://infinite.net/compliance/embedded) : your customers see your product while KYC and KYB run to network standard behind it, and when compliance needs more information, the request reaches your customer in your brand — as an API state your systems can track.


> Your customer relationship is the asset. The infrastructure underneath should strengthen it, not intermediate it.


05


## Third-party flows without renegotiating the model


When your platform moves money that belongs to your customers, regulators expect customer-level diligence on every one of them. On Infinite,[that program is the design center](https://infinite.net/funds-flow/third-party) : every customer gets a real account, screening and monitoring run across your whole portfolio,[AI assembles each case and a named analyst signs every decision](https://infinite.net/compliance/ai) — closing first-time reviews that traditionally take around 30 days in 1–2 — and a counterparty vetted once is vetted for every business on the network.


06


## When each fits


If the job is payout reach into long-tail corridors — mobile money, cash pickup, dozens of local rails — Noah has built genuine coverage. If the job is operating a money product on banking-grade primitives — individually titled accounts, bank-perimeter custody, your brand end to end, and a compliance program operated by the network —[that is the job Infinite is built for](https://infinite.net/funds-flow/third-party) .


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### Do my customers become Infinite's customers?


Your customers stay yours. Accounts are established under Infinite's regulated banking partners and operated under Infinite's compliance program, while onboarding, verification, and information requests all run through hosted flows in your brand — your customers see your product end to end.


### Which rails can one Infinite Account reach?


ACH, Fedwire, RTP, SWIFT, and stablecoin transfers in USDC, USDT, OUSD, and USDG, plus FX across GBP, EUR, MXN, and BRL — with routing that selects the right rail per corridor and wires reaching 170+ countries.


### Who holds custody of stablecoin balances on Infinite?


A chartered partner bank. Each Wallet Account is a bank-owned wallet established and controlled by the bank: your customer holds the balance, the bank holds the wallet and its keys, and key management never leaves the bank's custody perimeter.
